instructions: Grate the tomatoes on the large holes of a box grater and throw away the skins. Slice 1 of the garlic cloves thin.
Heat the olive oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Cook the sliced garlic for 30 seconds, then add the grated tomato and 1/2 tsp of the salt. Simmer on medium-low for 20 minutes, until thick.
Meanwhile, tear the bread into small pieces and soak it in 1/4 cup water for 2 minutes. Mince the other garlic clove and chop the parsley.
In a large bowl, mix the beef, pork, egg, soaked bread, minced garlic, parsley, 3/4 tsp of the salt and the pepper with your hands until just combined.
Shape the meat into about 8 flat oval patties. Spread the flour on a plate and coat both sides of each patty.

Heat the frying oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Fry the patties in two batches, 4 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through to 160°F, or no pink inside. Drain on paper towels and sprinkle with the remaining 1/4 tsp salt.
Spoon the simmered tomatoes over the patties and serve.
method_notes: Público's Spanish recipe (no rating shown) is the only one read that is the dish by name, so it leads as a fallback. It uses a beef and pork mix, bread soaked in milk, and a homemade tomato sauce; the milk is replaced with water so the dish stays dairy-free. The amounts are cut from 1 kg of meat to 1 1/2 lb for four. The sauce simmers while the patties are shaped and fried, so the total is about 32 minutes, 2 over the quick-dinner target.
